clue.text: Getting one out of ten in Latin, originally

definitions.text: Getting one out of ten in Latin, originally

parts.words: Getting one out of ten in Latin, originally
parts.note: the Roman army punished a mutinous unit by killing one soldier in every ten, and the word for it comes from Latin decimus, tenth

explanation.definitionFit: The word first meant the Roman penalty of executing every tenth man, before it came to mean heavy destruction.

clue.text: Wanted to be a schoolmaster, in fact

indicators.note: in places the schoolmaster inside the word for fact

parts.note: a deed is a fact or act, as in 'in deed'
pupils address a schoolmaster as sir

explanation.surface: Someone who wanted, in fact, to become a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired means longed for or wished for.

clue.text: Small group and you reportedly waste material for film

parts.note: a cell is a small group, as of activists

indicators.note: reportedly says the word you is spoken, and is written as the single letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word as written, said aloud
to lose is to waste, as in lose time

explanation.surface: A small group and you are said to be wasting film stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Celluloid, the base of early cinema film, is made from this plant fibre.

clue.text: Demonstrating over regulations leads to dismissal

parts.note: marching is demonstrating in protest
orders are regulations or rules

explanation.surface: A protest over rules ends in someone being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given one's marching orders is an idiom for being dismissed.

clue.text: Something like diet islanders elect to follow

definitions.text: Something like diet islanders elect to follow

parts.words: Something like diet islanders elect to follow
parts.note: a diet here is a parliament, and the islanders are those of the Isle of Man, who elect its members

explanation.definitionFit: It is the ancient parliament of the Isle of Man, a legislative assembly like a diet.

clue.text: Last longer than unfashionable guy

parts.note: out means out of fashion
a guy is a rope or wire that braces something, also called a stay

explanation.surface: An unfashionable fellow hangs around longer than others.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain longer than someone else.

clue.text: Victory hymn saint turned out

indicators.note: turned out means expelled, so the letter for saint is thrown out of the hymn word

parts.note: a psalm is a sacred song or hymn

explanation.surface: A saint is ejected after singing a victory hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm branch was the ancient token of triumph, so the palm stands for victory itself.

clue.text: Old man and fish

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic tribe that settled England in the fifth century
to fish with rod and line

explanation.definitionFit: It names one of the ancient English people and also means to fish.

clue.text: The smallest skirt a mother has

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
mum is a British word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother owns the tiniest skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The least possible amount is the lowest point of a range.

clue.text: Interference with digital input

parts.note: digital is read as using the digits of the hand, so the input is a poke of a fingertip into a pastry

explanation.definitionFit: Having this in something is an idiom for meddling or being involved in it.

clue.text: Glide across line in this sort of wind

indicators.note: the gliding word stretches across, so it sits on either side of the letter for line

parts.note: to soar is to glide high in the air

explanation.surface: A glider crossing a line on a windy day.
explanation.definitionFit: The solar wind is the stream of charged particles flowing out from the sun.

clue.text: Not being dressed up, having no engagements

definitions.meaning: with a free diary, no plans made

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both naked and having no appointments, two everyday idioms.

clue.text: Crude shed needed plaster

parts.note: rough means crude or unrefined
cast means shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready shed that needed its walls plastered.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is a coarse plaster of lime and gravel used to coat outside walls.

clue.text: Brief display of brilliance from English in Welsh county once

indicators.note: in places the English letter inside the old county's short name

parts.note: Glam is the abbreviation for Glamorgan, a former county of south Wales

explanation.surface: An Englishman shows flashes of brilliance in an old Welsh county.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief flash of light, or a fleeting show of something bright such as wit.

clue.text: Sank going round end of pier and perished in sea

indicators.note: the sinking word goes round, enclosing the selected letter

parts.note: downed means sank, as in sank a drink

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of pier

explanation.surface: Someone sank near the end of the pier and died at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sank' looks like the definition but it is DOWNED, as in downing a pint; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown is to die by suffocation under water, here in the sea.

clue.text: Branch of police force's main place of execution, historically

parts.note: the Yard is Scotland Yard, London's Metropolitan Police
an arm is a branch, as of a service or organisation

explanation.surface: A branch of the police where hangings once took place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open sea; sailors were once hanged from the end of a ship's yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutineers were hanged from the yard's tip at sea, making it a historical site of shipboard executions.

clue.text: Sanction a Euro with this modification

indicators.note: a modification is a change, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Approve a euro with this change.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction something is to give it official approval or permission.

clue.text: A playing partnership not all found alarming

parts.note: in bridge scoring, a partnership is recorded as we against they
some means a part, not all

explanation.surface: A bridge pair, not all of them present, find something frightening.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its older sense means inspiring awe or dread, hence alarming.

clue.text: It's definitely not a part of newspaper

definitions.meaning: the word a is the indefinite ..., a grammatical type that is not definite
a piece of writing printed in a paper

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a grammatical word like 'a' or 'the' and a newspaper piece.

clue.text: Solution that has soothing effect on viewer is nonsense

definitions.text: Solution that has soothing effect on viewer
definitions.meaning: a lotion for bathing sore eyes, the viewer being the eye

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a lotion for the eyes and slang for humbug.

clue.text: Island with a place for a long shot to get aquatic mammal

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man
in golf the drive, the longest shot, is played from the tee

explanation.surface: Someone on an island looks for a spot to take a long shot at an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea cow of warm coasts is a large plant-eating mammal living in water.

clue.text: Game for wits

definitions.meaning: a children's game played with small glass balls
as in losing one's ..., one's sanity

explanation.definitionFit: It names a children's game and is slang for mental faculties.

clue.text: People surrounded by snow — some turned up without appropriate equipment

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the turned word sits around the equipment
in a down clue turned up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a ski is equipment suited to snow

explanation.surface: Some people out in the snow turned up without the right kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives EMOS, the word some read backwards, which goes round SKI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit and Yupik peoples of the Arctic, an older and now often avoided name.

clue.text: Stuff that's sentimentally sweet, daughter concludes

parts.note: twee means cloyingly quaint or sentimental

explanation.surface: A daughter sums up something sickly sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is an old word for woven cloth, and tweed is a rough woollen fabric.

clue.text: Timepiece left by commercial traveller for consumer

indicators.note: left by means the travelling salesman departs from the watch word

parts.note: a repeater is a watch that chimes the time when a button is pressed
a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman leaves his watch behind for a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is one who consumes food.

clue.text: Lug most of the materials for the task in Offa's Dyke, say

parts.note: lug is slang for ear

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before trimming
work can mean the sewing or knitting one is busy with, the materials of the job in hand

explanation.surface: Hauling materials for building Offa's Dyke.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa's Dyke is an eighth-century bank and ditch along the England-Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of earth built as a boundary or defence is an example of such a construction.

clue.text: Howl — a cruel taws could produce more than one

indicators.note: could produce says the letters of the phrase can be rearranged into something new

parts.note: S is the plural ending, signalling more than one

explanation.surface: A cruel leather strap would make you howl.
explanation.walkthrough: A CRUEL TAWS rearranges to the plural, the answer with S added, hence 'more than one'. A taws is a Scottish leather strap once used to punish schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: To caterwaul is to howl or wail like a cat.

clue.text: The solid figure of a governess

definitions.meaning: a geometric solid with two identical end faces and parallelogram sides
Miss ... is the governess in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest

explanation.definitionFit: It names both a geometric solid and Wilde's fictional governess.

clue.text: Jug handles found largely on little pitchers

definitions.meaning: jug handles is jokey slang for protruding hearing organs
the proverb says little pitchers have big ..., meaning children overhear

explanation.definitionFit: Both readings point to the organs of hearing, via slang and a proverb.

clue.text: Simplicity of style pursued in speech by the head

indicators.note: in speech says the word for pursued is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: chased means pursued
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A headteacher's plain style is chased after in speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasteness of style means restraint and plainness, free of ornament.
